text: Hypothalamic galanin (GAL) stimulates feeding but differs from neuropeptide Y and agouti-related protein; it is unresponsive to food deprivation, corticosterone, glucose utilization, dietary carbohydrate and leptin. Instead, GAL in the paraventricular nucleus (PVN) tracks dietary fat and alcohol: it is stimulated by high-fat diet, alcohol and rising circulating lipids, and rises mid-active feeding cycle when triglycerides increase. Central GAL injection increases food and alcohol intake, with stronger feeding responses in fat-fed rats, implying non-homeostatic positive feedback circuits driving large meals, alcohol overconsumption and obesity. Separately, IL-18 knockout mice were overweight by 6 months and gained excess weight on low- and high-fat diets, ate more high-fat diet, and showed reduced whole-body energy expenditure with increased respiratory exchange ratios, suggesting IL-18 acts on basal metabolic rate across fasting/feeding and activity conditions.
